boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Carnifex Ferry record (September 10, 1861) in Operations in Western Virginia [June-December 1861]. The advance from Clarksburg, the September 11 occupation of Floyd's camp and the pursuit across the Gauley are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. NPS says Rosecrans moved three brigades south. Floyd says Rosecrans came with ten regiments, estimated at 8,000-9,000, against less than 2,000 engaged, and later that he had 1,800. Rosecrans reports Floyd's force as five regiments besides one driven in, with probably sixteen guns; papers found in camp showed at least five regiments, two batteries and a battalion of cavalry.
claims.rationale: Each side's estimate of the other and Floyd's own round figures; no return for either side. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.rationale: Ground from the two commanders' reports; no plan inspected. Floyd built the breastwork before the attack.

claims.value: The frozen commanders are Brigadier General John Floyd and Brigadier General William S. Rosecrans; the live page gives Rosecrans as Major General. Rosecrans says he directed the brigades and decided to withdraw from the woods at dusk; Floyd says he decided to recross the Gauley, his report being signed by his adjutant because of an injury; NPS says Floyd blamed Wise.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two commanders; no automatic sole credit and the live rank is not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says darkness halted several hours' fighting and Union artillery convinced Floyd to retreat. Floyd says he repulsed five assaults and recrossed without losing a gun; Rosecrans says the enemy crossed the Gauley in the night and his troops took the camp with prisoners, colors and stores.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 250 total; the live field reads 190 (US 158; CS 32). Rosecrans estimated 20 killed and 100 wounded on September 11 and gives 16 killed and 100 wounded in his September 21 report; Floyd reports only 20 wounded on his side.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: The brigade and regimental reports (Nos. 2-13), the No. 14 casualty statement, Wise's September 11 letter and the rest of his October 26 report were read at most in part and not selected.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Rosecrans's September 11 telegram and September 21, 1861 report (Official Records Series I, Volume V) are one family of interested Union accounts. Floyd's September 12, 1861 report, signed by his adjutant (same volume), is one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner Campaigns of the Civil War volume narrates this engagement; Nicolay's Chapter XII ends with McClellan's campaign in July.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
